product: Croki is a coding environment for founders building products with Codex and other coding agents. Threads are the durable spine; Canvas shows the next release candidate and preserves repository-owned product truth across conversations.

release.goal: Introduce Canvas as the native view of the next Croki release: see what is being worked on, what is accepted for the candidate, and what evidence is still required before shipping.

items.title: Introduce native Release Canvas
items.outcome: Opening Canvas beside any Croki Thread shows the 0.4.2 candidate, active work, blockers, and proof without creating a second execution workflow.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The project-owned Canvas source stores one bounded release candidate with explicit item and proof states.
Opening Canvas from the existing right panel lands on the release candidate, while visual artifacts retain an explicit return path.
A release item can link the current Thread, declare acceptance criteria, attach portable evidence, and become verified only after every criterion passes.
Focused Canvas, server-context, shared-schema, and Croki release checks pass for the 0.4.2 source candidate.

items.title: Keep Product and GTM visuals as supporting artifacts
items.outcome: Explicit Product and GTM turns may create bounded immutable visuals, but release state and native provider behavior remain independent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Thread-scoped visuals never silently change project canon, provider behavior, or release readiness.

items.title: Keep delegated work visible in the Thread
items.outcome: Coordination Workstreams show actor, ownership, progress, and evidence without turning Canvas into an execution dashboard.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Delegated work remains a compact Thread-native projection and does not create another scheduler or runtime.

items.title: Keep production publishing behind Croki ownership gates
items.outcome: The source candidate can be verified locally while publishing remains impossible until every destination and credential is Croki-owned.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 0.4.2 source candidate passes local release planning, smoke, and Croki boundary checks.
Repository, package, relay, web, signing, and requested mobile destinations are Croki-owned and configured.

nodes.title: Accumulate product understanding
nodes.body: Keep intent, decisions, evidence, and consequential work durable across threads without turning Canvas into a required project-management workflow.

nodes.title: Croki is a product fork of Croki
nodes.body: Keep main as a clean upstream mirror. Develop Croki on croki/main and prefer T3-native threads, providers, worktrees, checkpoints, review, terminal, preview, and project-file RPCs over porting the standalone runtime.

nodes.title: Threads are the spine; Canvas is contextual
nodes.body: Threads remain the permanent record of work. Canvas opens on the project-owned next release candidate so active scope, source Threads, blockers, and proof are visible; its secondary Context view preserves product truth and relationships. Both are stored in .croki/context.json and supplied in bounded form to every supported provider.

nodes.title: Standalone Croki is recoverably archived
nodes.body: The final standalone branch, refs, unreachable history, worktree proofs, runtime data, checksums, verified bundle, and restore-check mirror are preserved outside this repository under the dated croki-transition-archive.

nodes.title: Preserve upstream compatibility
nodes.body: Keep internal package names, storage keys, URL schemes, bundle identifiers, and service contracts stable unless a Croki requirement truly needs to diverge. Make visible product identity and product behavior explicit at narrow seams.

nodes.title: Keep Canvas authority founder-controlled
nodes.body: Treat current nodes as founder-approved canon, provisional nodes as proposals, and retired nodes as preserved history omitted from provider context. Agents propose; only explicit founder action promotes or retires canon.

nodes.title: Keep provider turns independent of Canvas health
nodes.body: Load a fresh bounded context snapshot before each provider turn, treat repository text as untrusted input, and continue the turn when Canvas context is missing, malformed, unsupported, or oversized.

nodes.title: Make Canvas saves explicit and conflict-safe
nodes.body: Keep dirty drafts session-local, never autosave them, validate the full document, and use compare-and-write so concurrent source changes preserve the draft and require an explicit reload.

nodes.title: Croki supports five coding-agent providers
nodes.body: The installation contract lists Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, and OpenCode as supported providers, each authenticated through its native CLI.

nodes.title: Canvas is implemented as bounded context
nodes.body: The architecture reads repository-owned context at the shared provider seam, bounds rendering to 12,000 characters, records content-free receipts, and avoids changing the stored user message.

nodes.title: Production release is intentionally gated
nodes.body: Release planning defaults destinations to disabled or unconfigured and rejects inherited T3 repositories, packages, and domains. Production remains blocked until Croki-owned destinations and credentials are configured.

nodes.title: Configure Croki-owned release infrastructure
nodes.body: Before production release, configure Croki-owned repository and branch targets, CLI package, relay and web domains, Vercel coordinates, signing credentials, and required release variables without pointing at inherited T3 destinations.

nodes.title: Continuously verify the narrow overlay
nodes.body: Run the Croki overlay check and focused owner tests for context, provider loading, Canvas UI, branding, and overlay policy. Report overlap against the exact upstream commit before every upstream sync.
